newsitem.title: UK: Gold touch lower in quiet Ldn precious market.
newsitem.headline: Gold touch lower in quiet Ldn precious market.

text.p: Gold prices edged lower on Friday but dealers said a long weekend in Britain could tempt a few shorts to take cover, establishing prices above the $340 buffer.
A landslide victory for the Labour Party in the British general election however was unlikely to agitate gold.
"The market is spending more time on looking at the effect of the Labour victory on their share portfolios rather than anything else," said a precious markets dealer in London.
Spot bullion fixed a touch higher at $339.80 an ounce from $339.25 as it struggled to keep its foothold above $340.00.
"I don't think we'll go anywhere too far," said the dealer.
This was because conditions were generally quiet in the precious metals complex with many European players absent as they bridged Thursday's May Day holiday with the weekend.
But silver stayed at the top of its range after gains racked up on Thursday gave it a sturdier outlook on the technical charts.
Gold's fortunes remained profoundly bearish with fears of central bank sales in the future keeping a tight lid on prices.
But traders said these bearish feelings could spark some short covering if professional dealers opted for a precautionary hedge before the weekend.
The key U.S. payrolls data expected at 1230 GMT today might be crucial in determining the extent of such covering.
"Unless something comes to their rescue from these figures then I think a few people may take back their shorts and we may establish ourselves back over $340," noted the London dealer.
But apart from a knee-jerk reaction, he doubted any fresh signs of inflationary pressures would produce gold rally.
"These days higher interest rates tend to imply a better opportunity for producers to sell gold," he said.
While gold stayed below $345 the risk of a slide to the low in February of $336.15 was technically intact. Upward moves were capped by $342.50 which held stubbornly in rallies last week.
Silver held steady though its advances were also limited.
It climbed back up to the top of its range and stood firmly at $4.74/$4.75 but range plays were still the favoured strategy.
Felder Rene, precious dealer at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said $4.60 was a critical level for silver. "If it breaks we have another 40 cents to go," he said earlier.
But charts were pointing to an upward ride, albeit cautiously.
Platinum and palladium stood a touch higher but they were more influenced by events, or lack of them, in Russia concerning delays in shipments to Japan.
Platinum gained 50 cents to $373.00/$374.00. The forward markets on both white metals were softer. --Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
